spanning-maze.look: Unwarped: a rectilinear perfect maze with even corridors, T-branches and dead ends; the kd (recursive division) rule gives long straight hierarchical walls, the quadtree rule a slightly more broken-up version of the same. The wide view shows the 2^L block structure as long walls, not as a visible tile grid. With warp 0.3 it becomes a brain-coral labyrinth that no existing node makes (Worley F2-F1 gives loops and closed cells). Zero set is between wall-distance and path-distance so cell centres always read +0.8 and lattice corners <= 0: the raw field is lattice-periodic by construction (axis ratio 400, seed sensitivity 0.18) and the maze only lives in the edge midpoints; a warp hides this completely. 3D isosurface at window 6: a tree of square-section pipes with elbows and dead ends, a genuinely new 3D look (3D maze / plumbing). Hilbert comparison: a regular non-branching meander whose corridors dead-end and fragment at block borders; after the same warp it is hard to tell from the maze visually, but it has no branches and no global connectivity.
spanning-maze.dims: 2D and 3D measured with one dimension-generic kd rule (3^D window, 18 edge tests in 2D, 81 in 3D); 4D is the same code path with hash4, not rendered
spanning-maze.range: [-1,1] clamped (out=0), mean ~0, no NaN, far coords fine. Values at cell centres are a constant 0.8.
spanning-maze.artifacts: lattice-periodic raw field; long straight coarse walls; top-level directed-forest join merges components only asymptotically (finite views of several 2^L blocks show a few infinite trees, still 0 enclosed pieces); 0-6 sub-pixel specks per 1200^2 image only when a warp pinches a corridor
spanning-maze.node_shape: Levels L, Rule {RecursiveDivision, Quadtree(2D)}, Output {Signed, CorridorDistance, WallDistance}, Gain, Feature Scale, Seed Offset; Hilbert not worth a mode (less capable, 1.7x slower)
spanning-maze.port_notes: Flood fill: 0 enclosed pieces both phases (3 seeds x 2 rules x warp 0/0.3); block-aligned windows: corridor exactly 1 piece in 6/6 (2D) and 2/2 (3D). Edge rule: l = trailing ones of c[ax]; l >= L top rule; else block id c[a]>>l (a<ax) or >>(l+1) (a>=ax), hash, open iff other coords' low bits equal the hashed gate. Lane-uniform loops; trailing-ones via float exponent or fixed loop; segment and face distances, two sqrts at the end.

critic.params: mode=0,L=5,cap=1,gain=2,warp=0.9,wfreq=0.125,w2=0.12,wf2=0.6 (warp stands in for an upstream DomainWarp pair); 3D cave view neg=1,warp=0.45,wfreq=0.25,cap=1,gain=2
critic.notes: The family's keeper, and the graph test backs that up. PingPong FBm, 1-8*Abs of warped Perlin, warped SineWave and warped Cellular F2-F1 all give loops or closed cells (10, 35, 45 enclosed pieces at 1024 px; PingPong has no zero crossing to threshold) and none has T-branches with dead ends at even corridor width. Dead ends 28%, branch 22%, 4-way 3%, measured. Relief with warp reads as a real ridged labyrinth, and the inverted 3D form is a block with tunnels. Faults: corridors live on a unit lattice so the raw field is periodic and needs a warp, recursive division leaves long straight walls in wide views, chiselled crease lines at corners in hillshade, and no tiling via 4D. Node shape: Output {Signed, CorridorDistance}, Rule {RecursiveDivision} only unless quadtree earns its keep (near identical look), fixed L around 8, with a doc note to warp at low frequency.
critic.improved: cap=1,gain=2: both distances capped at 0.5, which removes the white star spikes at 4-way junctions and the dark ones at wall crossings, and makes the range an analytic [-1,1] with centre lines at +-1. Two-scale warp (0.9 at f0.125 plus 0.12 at f0.6) replaces 0.3 at f0.5: FFT axis 14 vs 52, no row banding at window 24, corridor spacing now varies by region, topology kept. No node code needed for the warp. Merged rule (one hash per edge, top rule folded in, gate from hash bits): 5.4 vs 9.9 ns, flood fill 0 enclosed over 3 seeds. Tried and rejected: hashed jitter of corridor nodes and wall corners (jit param). jit 0.25 stays clean but keeps the rows (axis 135) at twice the scalar cost, and jit 0.3 breaks topology (34 corridor and 32 wall enclosed).

tournament.notes: Connectivity holds on my own union-find and flood fill: 0 cycles in 2D, 3D and 4D, 0 enclosed in both phases unwarped and at gentle warps, wall phase 1 piece in 3D. Multi-block windows are clipped forests, largest piece 22-38% at 512^2. Measured dead ends 28%, 3-way 22%, 4-way 3%. Existing-node graphs (PingPong FBm, Abs of warped Perlin, warped SineWave, warped Cellular F2-F1) gave loops or closed cells and no dead-end tree. The warped relief reads as a real ridged labyrinth, and the inverted 3D form is a block with tunnels. Faults: unit lattice needs a warp, long straight walls in wide views, chiselled creases at corners in hillshade, no tiling via 4D (needs a native period, not built). L has no visible effect at L >= 2 at window 40, so it can be fixed around 8.

artist-material.note: True mazes, circuit-board relief, and a wonderful 3D block. Unique, narrow, and warps well.

plan_node.expected_cost: Measured with fnlab bench, AVX2, 2D / 3D / 4D: 1.91 / 3.18 / 4.73 ns, against Perlin 0.90 / 2.10 / 4.16 and CellularDistance 3.90 / 12.42 / 41.52 in the same run. SSE41 3.14 / 6.30 / 9.00, AVX512 1.15 / 2.36 / 3.51. Same at any Levels and Output. Cap Distances False, the 3^D window search: 12.74 / 74.62 / 362.84. The Warped labyrinth preset with its two warps is 4.00 / 6.56 / 11.45.
plan_node.dims: 2D, 3D and 4D real: the edge graph read back through the node has 0 cycles and every block is a spanning tree in all three. GenTileable2D wraps with no seam, but the torus is a slice of the 4D maze, so it shows fragments: 3100 enclosed corridor pieces at 1024 px, Feature Scale 11, largest 0.3%. Native tiling is unsolved.
plan_node.range: Exactly [-1,1] by construction at the default Gain 2, measured -1.0000 to 1.0000 on every Output with and without the cap over up to 2M samples per dimension. Native range -1, 1 with no measured constant needed. Mean of Signed 0.000 / -0.410 / -0.622 and share above 0 is 50% / 22% / 9% in 2D / 3D / 4D, since corridors are lines and walls are faces.
notes: Warps stay in the graph, not the node. DomainWarpGradient keeps the guarantee up to Warp Amplitude 0.3x its Feature Scale (0 enclosed in 2D and 3D, at most 7 specks under 6 px), 0.4x gives 1-2 enclosed, 0.5x gives 5-13. Simplex warps are steeper for the same amplitude: DomainWarpSimplex breaks at 0.2x, DomainWarpSuperSimplex shows its first enclosed piece at 0.25x.
Capped path against the 3^D window: largest difference 2.4e-7 in 2D, 3D, 4D.

Capped distances need only the D edges towards the sample: a tree gives every cell centre an open edge, and a square of 4 edges cannot be open all round, so a wall always reaches the nearest corner lines.

The cut order is hashed per cube. A fixed axis order gave corridors a 1:2 share in 2D, 1:2:4 in 3D, 1:2:4:8 in 4D, with every even edge of the last axis forced open. Hashed: 0.50 / 0.50, 0.33 each, 0.25 each, at 35-50% more cost.

master.one_liner: Pointwise perfect maze from a hashed quadtree of spanning trees: corridors and walls are both trees, and the zero level set is one uninterrupted curve with no enclosed pieces.
master.look: Coral or brain-like labyrinth with wide even corridors and T-branches, rectilinear unless warped. Useful for guaranteed-reachable caves, dungeons, circuit patterns and reachable road or river masks. Measured over window 96, 3 seeds, 1500 px: both phases had 0 enclosed pieces unwarped. With warp 0.3 there are 0 enclosed pieces above 6 px, and 0 to 3 tiny pixel-scale pieces from 4-connected rasterisation at pinches.
master.algorithm: For edge between lattice cells a and a+1 along an axis: l = highest differing bit of a ^ (a+1). If l >= L, use a top-level binary-tree rule: each 2^L block links to its N or E neighbour by a hash bit at a hashed gate. Otherwise take the block of size 2^(l+1), hash it, omit one of the 4 joins between its children (leaving a spanning tree of the 4-cycle), and open only the hashed gate cell along each retained join. All tests are O(1) in the sample's window. Field: dPath = min distance to open edges between cell centres, dWall = min distance to closed wall segments, in a 3^D window. f = clamp((dWall - dPath)*k). Primal and dual trees interlock, so {f = 0} is a single curve. Wrap in a warp, since any homeomorphic warp preserves the topology.
master.why_new: Connectivity is guaranteed, not just likely, without flood fill, and no threshold of any existing node can guarantee it. Truchet gives loops, while Voronoi edges give a network with cycles and enclosed cells. Recursive-division mazes are global generators; the pointwise evaluation with infinite extent is the new part.
master.simd_plan: Highest differing bit: fixed loop over L (same for all lanes), or read the exponent of Convert(a^(a+1)) to float. In 2D about 12 edge tests x 1-2 hashes, plus segment distances; measured 5x perlin2 / 2.3x worley2 scalar. 3D: 54 edges in a 3^3 window, about 2x CellularDistance if restricted to the sample cell's neighbours; spanning tree of the cube's 8 children built by recursive halving: join two half-cubes by one hashed bridge per axis level. 4D by the same recursion, expensive at about 200+ edge tests.
master.continuity: C0, with kinks at the medial axis of distance fields. Measured c0ratio 8.
master.params: Levels L (int), Output (Signed Curve, Corridor Distance), Gain (float). Warp via upstream DomainWarp. Corridor width comes from thresholding.
master.risks: Long straight hierarchical walls and faint block lines at 2^L spacing are visible in the wide view; warp and larger L reduce them. Top-level binary-tree rule is directionally biased at the largest scale. 3D and 4D are unproven in code. Hard guarantee is lost if the user thresholds far from 0 (corridors can pinch only if threshold exceeds half-corridor width).
master.cost_note: In 2D about 12 edge tests x 1-2 hashes, plus segment distances; measured 5x perlin2 / 2.3x worley2 scalar.

barchan-field.look: Gray field and hillshade from above: aligned crescents with a sharp brink, horns trailing downwind, gentle stoss and steep slip face; kappa sets horn curvature (0.4 blunt arcs to 1.4 long trailing horns), stoss sets body length, supply 0.5 to 1 goes from scattered small crescents to a crowded field. Relief at hscale 20 with the rounded crest and ripples reads as a field of crescent mounds with dark slip faces and striated windward slopes; it sells 'barchan dunes from the air' reasonably, but less a desert: the horn wings are knife-thin fins, the interdune plain is dead flat, and in the dense setting the Max composition stacks crescents like scales instead of merging them into barchanoid ridges (no collision physics, as the judge warned). The transverse-dunes relief from the lattice-phasor family looks more like continuous sand; this one is the only thing that gives isolated crescents.
barchan-field.dims: 2D measured (3x3 window); 3D measured as time (two overlapping slabs, sin^2 fade, migration by travel/R): z-continuous but a crossfade between dune layers, not real migration; 4D not attempted
barchan-field.range: [-1, -0.34] at these params (flat plain at -1, dunes up to about 0.2 R * scale); mean -0.87; no NaN; far coords fine. Output max depends on rmax*h*scale, so VariableRange scaling would be needed.
barchan-field.artifacts: dune reach stoss*rmax must stay <= 1.2 cells or seams appear (1.44 gave c0ratio 3.2); polynomial smooth max lifted the plain by k/4 per cell (fixed by fading it at ground); ripple scaled by H jumped at the horn outline (fixed with Hv); FFT oriented streaks, axis ratio 25
barchan-field.node_shape: Wind Angle, Sand Supply (hybrid: density and size), Size Min/Max, Jitter, Height, Horn Curvature, Stoss Length, Slip Length, Crest Round, Ripple Amount/Frequency, Smooth Merge; honest as a 2D node, the time-crossfade 3D form is weak
barchan-field.port_notes: Per cell: hash, jittered centre, R, rotate (p-c) by wind, t=v/R, Hv=H(1-t^2), brink kappa R t^2, toe -stoss R sqrt(1-t^2), s=(u-ut)/(ub-ut), z=min(Hv s^1.5, Hv-(u-ub)H/(lee R)) with optional polynomial smooth min at the crest; Max or faded smooth max smax=max+h^2k/4*sat(min/k). Slip slope is relative to R, not world units.

critic.notes: Top-down and relief are distinctive and nothing in the existing nodes makes discrete oriented crescents. But it is one landform, 3D is a time crossfade rather than a volume or migration, there is no 4D or tiling, native range is about [-1,-0.2] and needs normalising, and at 20+ ns it is well outside building-block cost. Worth including as a showcase or example; not a general node. FFT shows oriented streaks (axis 25-43), which is the shared wind direction, not a lattice fault; c0 is clean.
critic.improved: Added: hp (envelope (1-t^2)^(1..1.5), reuses the existing sqrt, tapers horn fins), faded spatial supply (sv, sfreq, sfade: swarms and bare corridors without seams), wind sampled per sample position (wv, wvf, one Perlin instead of nine), interdune ripple rg and swell, slip face lee 0.42 so the slope is closer to the 33 degree angle of repose, wider size range. First attempt hp=0.7 was worse: horns went and dunes read as dark triangles, so I backed off to 0.3. Added a render (same projection as relief, sand ramp, adjustable sun). Helped a lot.

tournament.notes: Sells a desert from the air and in oblique relief. Remaining tells: same stamped profile on every dune, dense regions overlap rather than merge into true barchanoid ridges, hard slip faces. Measured AVX2 20-22 ns, 16.3 ns without ripple, port agrees with scalar. That is 18-25x Perlin and 4-6x Cellular 2D, which is why port is 6. Critic params: c0ratio 7.79; AVX2 not measured for them, estimate 22-27 ns. Existing-node crescents came out as thin arcs in a Voronoi web, not discrete dunes. One landform, 3D is a time crossfade, no 4D or tiling, native range about [-1,-0.2] needs normalising. Showcase rather than a general node.

master.one_liner: Analytic crescent dunes with a true constant-angle slip face, combined by Max so rising sand supply merges isolated barchans into barchanoid and transverse ridges.
master.look:
Hillshade reads immediately as barchan dunes seen from above, all aligned with the wind and with shaded crescents. Varying curvature gives parabolic or transverse shapes. In 3D, the same kernel gives scalloped shell shapes.
[PolarKernelField (Barchan), lattice-kernels] Barchan dune fields, wind-driven snow sastrugi, shark scales, directional crag and tail. Prototyped: distinct crescent horns with sharp lee side on a flat ground at density 0.7; density 1 merges into fields of sails. The hillshade is immediately sand-like.
master.algorithm:
Lattice with jitter and staggered rows. For each cell in the 3x3 window, take (u,v)=rotate(p-c, wind(p)), a local rotation about the dune's own centre, so spatially varying wind causes no far-field shear. Size H from hash*SandSupply(p); R=k1*H; toe length Lt=k2*H.
Across-wind: if |v|<R, H_v=H*(1-(v/R)^2). Brink: ub(v)=kappa*v^2 (horns trail downwind). Toe: ut(v)=-Lt*sqrt(1-(v/R)^2).
Height: for u<ub, s=(u-ut)/(ub-ut), z=H_v*s^1.5 (stoss). For u>=ub, z=max(0,H_v-Slip*(u-ub)) (lee), and Slip is a world-space slope constant. out=SmoothMax over candidates.
Second scale: add ripples only on stoss, perpendicular to the wind, weighted by s*(1-s), and none on the slip face, giving non-additive fractal detail. SandSupply controls both size and existence.

[BarchanField, nature-phenomena] H=small base. For each cell in the 3^D window: v=x-p_i; R=Rmin+Rrange*r3; u=(v.w)/R (along wind); t=|v-(v.w)w|/R (across wind: |perp| in 2D, radial distance in the plane perpendicular to w in 3D); sc=u-curve*t^2 (crest is a parabola); env=saturate(1-t^2)^0.75; up=saturate(1+sc/Lw)^1.5 (windward, Lw=1.3); dn=saturate(1-sc/Ls) (slip face, Ls=0.28); pr=Select(sc<0,up,dn)*env*R; H=max(H,pr). Add time by offsetting positions along wind with a speed that scales inversely with R, to make small dunes migrate faster.
master.why_new: Sawtooth or warped-ridge approaches give neither crescents nor a slip angle independent of scale, and no existing node has a mechanism that moves between isolated and connected dune topologies under a single hybrid.
master.simd_plan:
9 kernels with Select masks, one sqrt per kernel; about CellularDistance 2D, 4-8 ns, about 5x Perlin. 3D: treat z as time, moving c by wind*z*V/H within a per-cell lifetime fade (larger dunes slower), or 3D cells at 27 kernels. 4D: 81 is expensive; use (x,y) cells plus crossfade or accept no tiling.
[BarchanField, nature-phenomena] Cell loop with max and Select; no atan. Estimated 6 ns in 2D (5x Perlin, 1.5x CellularDistance), 20 ns in 3D, 60-80 ns in 4D. Wind direction is a member or hybrid. Use x^1.5 as x*sqrt(x), or an integer power in the port.
master.continuity: C0: H_v=0 at |v|=R, s=0 at toe and lee reaches 0 by clamp. Slip face is a sharp but continuous crease, as in nature. Dune extent must stay within the window, so R and the downwind reach are clamped to 1 cell.
master.params: Wind Angle (hybrid), Sand Supply (hybrid), Size Jitter, Horn Curvature kappa, Stoss Length, Slip Slope (float), Ripple Amount and Wavelength.
master.risks:
Not tested. Max composition does not produce real collisions. Fully transverse ridges require R at window limit, so high supply may still look like a chain of crescents. Elevation slope depends on Feature Scale, so Slip must be defined in output-per-world units and may need rescaling.
[BarchanField, nature-phenomena] Kernel reach must fit within the window at maximum R, or seams appear at cell edges. Slip-face steepness aliases at low sampling rates. Physical accuracy is stylised, not simulated. Only the 2D form was prototyped; the 3D use is speculative.
master.cost_note: 9 kernels with Select masks, one sqrt per kernel; about CellularDistance 2D, 4-8 ns, about 5x Perlin.
master.variant_notes: Option: per-dune wind sampled at the lane gives no far-field shear because rotation is about each dune's own centre. Slip slope must be defined in world units.

master.one_liner: Pointwise Hilbert space-filling curve: exact distance to the curve polyline (maze/circuit corridors with width), position-along-curve value, and hashed adaptive depth for mixed corridor widths; 3D via Skilling's algorithm.
master.look: A dense labyrinth of corridors that never cross, filling space at one scale, or with adaptive depth a circuit-board/Greek-key texture mixing wide and narrow corridors and dead ends. Along mode gives a continuous path value, turning it into 'a single river that visits every cell'. Distinct from everything on the sheet (nothing produces non-crossing connected corridors). Uses: mazes, circuitry, ornaments, sci-fi panelling, wall masks for dungeon generators, 3D 'pipes' volumes.
master.algorithm:
Scale p so the top cell is [0,2^n). Per lane integers X=floor(x), Y=floor(y) clamped by tiling the top cell with a hashed per-top-cell flip/rotation to avoid a visible period.
  xy2d (Wikipedia form, branch-free): d=0; for s=2^(n-1) down to 1: rx=(X&s)>0; ry=(Y&s)>0; d += s*s*((3*rx)^ry); rot(s,X,Y,rx,ry) using Select (if ry==0: if rx==1 {X=s-1-X; Y=s-1-Y}; swap X,Y).
  d2xy similarly for dPrev=d-1 and dNext=d+1 (clamped) giving the centres cPrev, cNext of the neighbouring leaves (they are 4-adjacent, distance exactly 1 cell).
  Inside the current leaf the curve is the polyline  mid(c,cPrev) -> c -> mid(c,cNext). dist = min(segDist(p, mid1, c), segDist(p, c, mid2)) in cell units.
  Outputs: Corridor = 1 - 2*smoothstep(0, Width, dist); Distance = dist; Along = valueNoise1D(d * AlongFreq / 4^n) (smooth value that varies along the path, exposes the maze as a gradient); Index = d / 4^n.
  Adaptive depth: n_lane = Select(frozen_at_level_k ...) implemented by computing d at the full depth and masking lower bits (d >> 2*(n-k) << 2*(n-k)) plus centre at that coarser cell; neighbours at the coarse depth. Joints between depths are offset by a quarter cell (dead-end look).
  3D: AxesToTranspose/TransposeToAxes (Skilling 2004) on 3 coordinates, same polyline construction with 6-adjacent neighbours.
master.why_new: Space-filling corridors are impossible from any graph of existing nodes; the exact pointwise distance construction (neighbouring leaves via d2xy) makes it a real generator, not a lookup. Hashed depth makes it a multi-scale structure.
master.simd_plan: Three integer traversals of n levels (xy2d + 2x d2xy), each level ~12 int ops with Selects, all lane-uniform loops; n<=12 in 2D, n<=10 in 3D (fits int32). Then 2 segment distances. Estimated 2D n=8: ~3-4x Perlin; 3D Skilling ~2x that. 4D: Skilling generalises to any dimension (loop over 4 axes), fine for tiling.
master.continuity: Distance/Corridor are C0 (true distance field to a polyline). Along and Index are piecewise constant per leaf (discontinuous), as intended.
master.params: Depth int, Width hybrid, Output enum {Corridor, Distance, Along, Index}, Adaptive StopProb hybrid, MinDepth, Along Frequency, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
master.risks: Top-level period of 2^n cells; hide with per-top-cell hashed symmetry (8 dihedral variants) at the cost of corridors not connecting across top cells (acceptable: a dead end). Integer precision limits depth. Adaptive joints are offset by design.
master.cost_note: Three integer traversals of n levels (xy2d + 2x d2xy), each level ~12 int ops with Selects, all lane-uniform loops; n<=12 in 2D, n<=10 in 3D (fits int32). Estimated 2D n=8: ~3-4x Perlin; 3D Skilling ~2x that.

light-cone-ca.look: Cave rule (B5678/S45678 = 9-cell majority vote): clean rounded blobs with concave bays, uniform blob scale and a constant-width soft edge from the 4x4 tent, no specks after 3-4 generations; Fill 0.38 gives isolated islands, 0.5 bicontinuous, 0.62 isolated lakes. Side by side with a soft-thresholded 3-octave Perlin FBm the CA is more pebble-like and even, FBm has tendrils and variable edge softness; the difference is real but modest. Maze rule B3/S12345 at 10 generations is a grainy rectilinear circuit texture, not corridors (the rule needs far more generations than a window affords); Coral and Life at 5-6 generations are sparse scattered blobs. Pyramid mode (4 levels, flip 0.25, 2 gens per level) in the 32-unit wide view is a chunky fractal coastline with islands and lakes and crisp edges, the most distinctive look here, but it costs ~30x Perlin scalar. 3D isosurface: porous blob solid, like a thresholded low-pass noise; 1 generation is noisier than 2.

light-cone-ca.range: [-1,1] clamped, mean ~0 at fill 0.5, no NaN, far coords fine, seed sensitivity 0.985

light-cone-ca.node_shape: Generations, Rule enum {Cave45, Vote, Maze, Coral, Life, Diamoeba, Custom}, Birth/Survive masks, Fill (hybrid-capable), Sharpness, Smoothing radius, Output {Smooth, Bilinear, Cell}; Pyramid Levels + Flip as a second mode; 3D thresholds on 26 neighbours
light-cone-ca.port_notes: Exactness verified by brute-force grid CA: 0 mismatches in 8 configs. Port layout is in the prototype: W int32v rows per lane, bit-sliced full-adder neighbour counts over shifted rows, rule as OR of equality masks; output cells at offsets -1..2 keep the 4x4 tent continuous; stack-only, no heap. A column-sum adder tree would halve the logic.

critic.params: gens=4,rule=0,fill=0.5,cs=4,sharp=6,rad2=3.2 (unchanged). The recipe that replaces it: Max(LHS=Min(LHS=Multiply(LHS=SuperSimplex(Feature Scale=95),RHS=20),RHS=1),RHS=-1)
critic.notes: The technical claim is true and I confirmed it harder than asked: this is an exact CA as a pure function, and the port layout works. The eye test fails: the default look is available from existing nodes at about a tenth of the cost, and 3D is no better than a SuperSimplex isosurface at 3.9 ns. Lattice imprint is mild, FFT axis 15-22 with a ring at the tent frequency, a few faint single-cell dots at 4 gens. The rules that do look different need 10+ gens, which is 170 ns and up, and their output is grainy. Keep the verify code as a reference for anyone asking whether pointwise CA is possible; do not ship a node.
critic.improved: Tried 8 more rules at 8 gens (anneal, day and night, stains, walled cities, coagulations, assimilation, 2x2, mazectric) and an age output (fraction of generations alive). Most are grainier thresholded noise. Walled cities gives holes in both phases, mazectric gives axis-aligned stripe patches that the tent filter renders gray; both cost about 90-330 ns (gens 8 is an estimate between measured gens 6 and 10, gens 14 an extrapolation). Nothing beat the original enough to change the gallery.

tournament.notes: Exactness confirmed independently, pyramid included, and the AVX2 port matches scalar exactly. Measured AVX2: gens 2 12.3, gens 3 19.4, gens 4 29.6, gens 6 about 57 ns. Branch-free is proven, cheap is not, which is why port is only 4. The default look is available from existing nodes at about a tenth of the cost, and 3D (estimate 92-290 ns) looks no better than a 3.9 ns SuperSimplex isosurface. The 4-level pyramid has a chunky coast with flecks that my FBm clamp graphs did not match exactly, but that is a small gain at about 205 ns (estimate). Do not ship a node.

master.one_liner: Runs an exact cellular automaton (cave rule, maze rule, Life) for k generations on a hash-seeded infinite grid per sample by computing only the (2k+3)^2 light cone with bit-sliced logic, optionally as a multi-resolution pyramid.
master.look: Verified in prototype. 4-5 rule: rounded cave blobs with concave bays and no specks, more compact than thresholded noise and no axis feel after tent smoothing. Maze rule: rectilinear circuit-like corridors. Pyramid: chunky fractal coast with islands and crisp edges, not the tendrils of thresholded FBm. Good for roguelike caves, dungeon masks, microbial colonies, circuit patterns.
master.algorithm: State at (cell,t) depends only on cells within radius t at t=0, so it is exact, stateless and seamless. For sample cell c, W=2(k+1)+1: build W rows as int32v bit-rows, each bit = hash(seed,c+offset) < Fill. For each generation run a bit-sliced neighbour count (full adders over the 8 shifted row copies, 4-bit count across all columns simultaneously), apply a birth/survive rule table as boolean logic. Take the final 4x4 cells around the sample, weight by radial tent (1-d^2/3.2)^2, output Clamp((sum/ws-0.5)*Sharp). Pyramid mode: L levels, each level's cell = parent bit XOR (hash<Flip), then 2 generations; patch radius stays constant across levels. Prototypes: dyn_lens mode=31,gens=4 (4-5 rule); mode=31,gens=5,birth=8,survive=62 (maze); mode=35,L=5,flip=0.25,cs=1.5 (pyramid).
master.why_new: Cave CA is the canonical thing that everyone thinks needs a grid pass. Here it is the same exact automaton as a pure function of position, with GenPositionArray support and identical output at any scale. Rule choice opens a pattern family that no noise covers (maze corridors).
master.simd_plan: Bitboards per lane: rows of int32v with shifts and boolean ops; full adder neighbour count about 30 vector ops per row per generation. 2D gens=3, W=9: 81 cell hashes plus about 800 ops, estimate about 25 ns. Pyramid L=4 with k=2 and radius 7, about 60 ns. 3D gens=2, W=7: 49 rows of 7 bits, 26-neighbour adders, estimate about 150 ns. 4D gens=1 only (W=5, 625 bits), about 300 ns, or offer 4D as expensive. Per-node boolean rule tables.
master.continuity: Discontinuous at Sharp high; Lipschitz at Sharp low because the tent over 4x4 cells moves smoothly with fx, fy, but cell changes at lattice lines are covered by tent going to 0 at the 4x4 border only approximately, so check with fnlab. Treat as C0 with small seams to tune the kernel.
master.params: Generations int, Rule enum (Cave45, Maze, Coral, Custom B/S masks), Fill float (hybrid would alter pattern locally, cheap and useful), Sharpness, Levels and Flip for pyramid.
master.risks: Short generations are not enough to converge slow rules (maze at 5 gens is partial). Axis alignment returns with crisp sharpness or maze rules, so usually pair with a warp. High dimensions are costly. Patch is per-lane stack data, which is new territory for FastNoise but legal (no heap).
master.cost_note: 2D gens=3, W=9: 81 cell hashes plus about 800 ops, estimate about 25 ns. 3D gens=2, W=7: 49 rows of 7 bits, 26-neighbour adders, estimate about 150 ns.
